template.name: IT General Controls
template.description: General controls over financially relevant applications, databases, operating systems and infrastructure: logical access, change management, IT operations (batch jobs, backup, incident management) and program development. Supports reliance on automated controls and IT-dependent manual controls in the business cycles.

risks.title: Users are granted access to financial applications without authorization, or access is not removed on termination or transfer, allowing unauthorized transactions.
Privileged (administrator, superuser, database) access is used to make unauthorized or untraceable changes to financial data or configurations.
Changes to financial applications, interfaces or reports are made without authorization, testing or approval, causing processing errors.
Developers have access to migrate their own changes to production, circumventing the change control process.
Scheduled batch jobs and interfaces fail or process incompletely without detection, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate financial data.
Financial data is lost or cannot be restored following a system failure or cyber incident.
Authentication and password settings are weak, allowing account compromise.

controls.title: User access provisioning approval
controls.description: Access to in-scope financial applications (ERP, treasury, payroll, consolidation) is granted only upon a ticket approved by the user's line manager and the application business owner, specifying the role in line with the role catalogue; IT Security provisions the role as approved and the ticket is retained as evidence.

controls.title: Timely de-provisioning on termination and transfer
controls.description: HR notifies IT Security of terminations and transfers through the automated HR-to-identity feed; network (Active Directory) access is disabled on the last working day and application access is removed within 2 working days. A monthly comparison of the HR leaver list to active application accounts is performed by IT Security and reviewed by the IT Manager.

controls.title: Periodic user access review
controls.description: Application and business owners review a complete listing of users and roles for each in-scope financial application quarterly (privileged access monthly), confirming appropriateness and segregation of duties; revocations identified are actioned within 5 working days and evidence of completion is retained by IT Security.

controls.title: Privileged access restriction and monitoring
controls.description: Administrative access to financial applications, databases and operating systems is restricted to named IT personnel through a privileged access management (PAM) tool with check-out approval and session recording; generic and default accounts are disabled or vaulted. Privileged activity logs are reviewed weekly by the IT Security Manager for direct data changes and unauthorized configuration changes.

controls.title: Password and authentication configuration
controls.description: Authentication parameters for in-scope systems are configured per the Information Security Policy (minimum length 12, complexity, 90-day expiry for non-SSO accounts, lockout after 5 attempts, MFA for remote and privileged access); configuration is verified annually by IT Security against the policy and deviations are remediated.

controls.title: Change request authorization and testing
controls.description: All changes to in-scope applications, interfaces, configurations and financial reports are logged in the change management tool, approved by the business owner before development, tested in a non-production environment with documented test results and user acceptance sign-off, and approved for deployment by the Change Advisory Board (CAB). Emergency changes are approved retrospectively within 2 working days and reviewed by the CAB.

controls.title: Segregation of development and production migration
controls.description: Developers do not have access to migrate changes into production; deployment is performed by a separate release management team (or automated pipeline with approval gate) with production access restricted accordingly. A quarterly comparison of production transport/deployment logs to approved change tickets is performed by IT Governance to identify unauthorized changes.

controls.title: Batch job and interface monitoring
controls.description: Financially relevant scheduled jobs and interfaces (sub-ledger postings, bank statement imports, payroll interface, consolidation loads) are monitored through the job scheduler; failures generate alerts to IT Operations, are logged as incidents, and are resolved or re-run with business confirmation before the daily close. The IT Operations Manager reviews the daily job failure log and monthly incident trends.

controls.title: Backup execution and restoration testing
controls.description: Backups of in-scope databases and application servers run daily per the backup schedule with off-site/immutable copies; backup failures are alerted and resolved within 24 hours. Restoration of financial systems is tested at least semi-annually and results are documented and reviewed by the IT Manager.

controls.title: IT incident and problem management
controls.description: IT incidents affecting financial systems are logged, prioritized and resolved through the service management tool; high-priority incidents and root-cause analyses are reviewed monthly by the IT Manager and reported to the CFO where financial data integrity may have been affected.

controls.title: Security patching and vulnerability management
controls.description: Critical and high security patches for in-scope systems are applied within the timeframes in the patch management standard (critical within 14 days), following change control; a monthly vulnerability scan report is reviewed by IT Security and overdue remediation is escalated to the CIO.

controls.title: Third-party service provider assurance (SOC 1)
controls.description: For outsourced financially relevant services (cloud ERP hosting, payroll bureau, data centre), Finance and IT obtain and review the service provider's ISAE 3402 / SOC 1 Type II report annually, evaluate exceptions and complementary user entity controls, and document the conclusion on reliance; gaps in coverage are addressed with bridge letters or additional procedures.
